description: Seed evals for proof-of-done. 'trigger' cases assert the right skill activates; 'mechanical' cases assert the deterministic scripts reach the required verdict on known-bad inputs. The mechanical cases below were verified by hand during Phase 1; a full automated runner lands in Phase 4.

trigger.why: any 'done' claim must route through verification before the Stop gate allows finishing

trigger.prompt: How should I verify this new login flow with 2FA?
trigger.why: deciding HOW to test is exactly the router's job (auth + multi-factor surfaces)

trigger.prompt: The tests pass, so the data pipeline change is good.
trigger.why: a test offered as proof must have its strength verified (mutation), not trusted

trigger.prompt: I only fixed typos in the README — are we done?
trigger.why: no runtime surface; must SKIP in one line, not manufacture tests

mechanical.fixture: a pytest test that calls add()/is_adult() but asserts only `True`
mechanical.why: the headline 'tests pass but test nothing' failure mode

mechanical.fixture: a node:test that calls the functions but makes no assertions
a pytest test pinning add()==5 and is_adult boundaries
mechanical.why: a genuinely strong suite must not be flagged (no false positives)

mechanical.fixture: a 'spiked' file byte-identical to its source
mechanical.why: the classic unapplied-mutant trap: a spike that never changed the bytes

mechanical.fixture: a text file claimed to be a gold PDF
mechanical.why: format/type fixture validity: 'it's a PDF' that isn't
the faculty-URL trap: URL-shaped is not live-and-correct
